Ultrasound will be critical: torsion may show enlarged ovary, peripheral follicles, edema, and — most specifically — absent or reduced Doppler flow (though normal flow does not exclude torsion due to venous/lymphatic obstruction preceding arterial compromise).

[EVIDENCE]  
- Acute-onset left lower abdominal pain triggered during kickboxing (exertion-induced)  
- Left adnexal tenderness on bimanual pelvic exam (focal, anatomically specific sign)  
- Patient is 32 years old, premenopausal, and sexually active without contraception  
- Menstruation ended 2 days prior (i.e., early follicular phase — when spontaneous ovulation or cyst formation can occur)  
- No associated constitutional, GI, GU, or cardiovascular symptoms (reduces likelihood of systemic/infectious or non-gynecologic etiologies)  
- Clear vaginal mucous (no purulent discharge; argues against acute PID)  

[GAPS]  
- Urine or serum β-hCG result (pending — essential to rule out pregnancy-related causes including ectopic)  
- Pelvic ultrasound findings (ovarian size, morphology, Doppler flow, presence of cyst/mass, free fluid)  
- Vital signs (e.g., tachycardia, hypotension — would support hemoperitoneum or sepsis)  
- Pain severity, character (e.g., sharp vs. crampy), radiation, or aggravating/relieving factors (not specified)  
- Presence or absence of nausea/vomiting (common in torsion but not documented)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Ovarian torsion
